title: Finished and shipped my retro horror game 'STILL LIVE' on itch.io using Claude Code + MCP for Unity. Here’s what the workflow looked like (Playable link inside)
author: Antique-Constant-102
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev,

I just released my indie horror game, **STILL LIVE**, on itch.io. Having a formal background in game development, I wanted to see how far I could push current AI workflows to overcome standard solo-dev bottlenecks and actually take a project from raw concept all the way to a finished, published release.

**The Game Concept** You play as a streamer live at your desk on a dark, rainy night. The gameplay uses a fixed-camera view (inspired by *Five Nights at Freddy's* and *I'm on Observation Duty* mechanics).

* **The Loop:** Every time lightning strikes, the stream cuts out. You have to quickly inspect your room and decide on your monitor: is everything normal, or has an anomaly appeared?
* **Mechanics:** 32 unique, handmade anomalies (ranging from subtle, eerie visual shifts to full jumpscares), a dynamic viewer count system that acts as your score multiplier, and a retro PS1 aesthetic built in Unity 6 (URP) with a custom post-processing shader.

**The Workflow: Claude Code + MCP for Unity** Rather than just asking an LLM for isolated C# code snippets, I used **Claude Code integrated via MCP (Model Context Protocol) for Unity**. This let the AI interact directly with the editor environment:

* **Scene & State Awareness:** Reading scene hierarchy, inspecting game objects, and modifying parameters directly within the Unity project structure.
* **Modular Anomaly Pipeline:** Every anomaly inherits from a clean base class (`AnomaliaBase`). This allowed us to iterate fast and build 32 distinct mechanical behaviors (procedural audio triggers, light flicker timing, dynamic spider pathfinding, etc.) without cluttering the core game loop.
* **Dev Tools & Automated Testing:** Setting up custom internal verification tools (like a dev suite to run automated passes through all 32 anomalies) so I could test edge cases, timers, and state resets without having to manually play through 10 rounds every single time.

Having a background in game design and programming was crucial here—it made directing the AI much faster, allowed me to catch edge cases early (like managing static variables across play state options), and ensured the architecture stayed clean.

**Playable Link & Q&A** The game is completely finished, fully localized in English and Spanish, and features a full night cycle plus a gallery mode to view all anomalies once completed.

🎮 **Play it on itch.io:**[https://zraner.itch.io/still-live](https://zraner.itch.io/still-live)

I’d love for you to give it a run and leave any feedback or bug reports. If anyone is curious about setting up or working with Claude Code + MCP for Unity on a real project pipeline, feel free to ask!
